reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive defect of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein (HADHA/HADHB genes) that carries out three steps of long-chain fatty-acid beta-oxidation; isolated LCHAD deficiency is a common subtype
Presents across a spectrum from severe neonatal cardiomyopathy and hypoketotic hypoglycaemia to a milder later-onset phenotype with episodic rhabdomyolysis and a progressive peripheral neuropathy
Fasting or intercurrent illness precipitates hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, liver dysfunction and metabolic decompensation
LCHAD deficiency is distinctively associated with a progressive pigmentary retinopathy and peripheral neuropathy not usually seen in other fatty-acid oxidation defects
Carrying an affected fetus is linked to maternal HELLP syndrome and acute fatty liver of pregnancy, so a maternal obstetric history is an important clue
Blood acylcarnitines show elevated long-chain hydroxyacylcarnitines, detectable on newborn screening
Management centres on avoidance of fasting, a low long-chain-fat diet with medium-chain triglyceride substitution, and prompt glucose during catabolic stress
reference.pathophysiology: The mitochondrial trifunctional protein is a hetero-octamer of alpha (HADHA) and beta (HADHB) subunits that performs the last three enzymatic steps of long-chain fatty-acid beta-oxidation: long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCHAD) and long-chain 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activities. Deficiency blocks energy production from long-chain fats, so during fasting or illness tissues cannot generate adequate ATP or ketones, producing hypoketotic hypoglycaemia and accumulation of toxic long-chain hydroxyacyl intermediates. These intermediates injure the heart, skeletal muscle, liver, peripheral nerves and retina. Reduced fatty-acid oxidation in the fetus and placenta also underlies the associated maternal liver disease of pregnancy.
additionalInvestigations: Plasma acylcarnitine profile showing elevated long-chain 3-hydroxyacylcarnitines
Blood glucose, ketones and free fatty acids during acute episodes to demonstrate hypoketotic hypoglycaemia
Creatine kinase and myoglobinuria assessment during suspected rhabdomyolysis
Echocardiography and ECG to evaluate cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia
Ophthalmological review and nerve conduction studies for retinopathy and neuropathy
HADHA/HADHB molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
redFlags: Neonatal cardiomyopathy with hypoketotic hypoglycaemia and collapse
Acute rhabdomyolysis with risk of renal impairment during illness or exertion
Arrhythmia or cardiac decompensation during metabolic crises
Maternal HELLP syndrome or acute fatty liver of pregnancy prompting evaluation of the infant
reference.prognosis: The severe neonatal cardiomyopathic form carries high mortality, whereas milder phenotypes may be managed with diet and fasting avoidance; however, progressive retinopathy and peripheral neuropathy can cause long-term morbidity even with good metabolic control.
pitfalls: Missing hypoketotic hypoglycaemia by not measuring ketones alongside glucose
Failing to consider the diagnosis in a mother with HELLP or acute fatty liver of pregnancy
Overlooking the evolving retinopathy and neuropathy that distinguish LCHAD/MTP deficiency
Allowing prolonged fasting or high long-chain-fat intake that precipitates decompensation
references: Scriver's OMMBID: Disorders of Mitochondrial Fatty Acid Oxidation
Saudubray, Baumgartner & Walter, Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment
management: Dietary therapy is the mainstay: a low long-chain-fat diet supplemented with medium-chain triglycerides that bypass the enzyme block, together with a high complex-carbohydrate intake
Strict avoidance of fasting with frequent feeds and an emergency regimen of extra carbohydrate during intercurrent illness, and intravenous dextrose when oral intake fails
Docosahexaenoic acid supplementation to slow the LCHAD-associated pigmentary retinopathy, with carnitine used cautiously only if deficient
Prompt treatment of acute rhabdomyolysis with intravenous fluids and hydration to protect renal function
Cardiac surveillance with echocardiography and ECG and heart-failure or arrhythmia treatment for the cardiomyopathic form
Regular ophthalmological review for retinopathy and nerve conduction studies for peripheral neuropathy

Multidisciplinary metabolic team follow-up with a specialist dietitian, autosomal recessive genetic counselling with newborn screening and family testing, and awareness of the maternal risk of HELLP and acute fatty liver of pregnancy
